skill.name: self-improvement
skill.description: Captures agent learnings, command failures, user corrections, and feature requests in workspace learning logs for later review.
skill.summary: Maintains structured learning logs and reminders for AI coding workflows.
skill.author: peterskoett

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives in context: they are mostly Markdown backticks, documentation URLs, home-directory setup examples, and secret-avoidance text. No evidence of malware, credential exfiltration, or unauthorized runtime network activity was found. The main residual concern is durable prompt-memory poisoning through promotion of untrusted learnings into future agent instruction files.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user review before writing or promoting content into CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, SOUL.md, or TOOLS.md.

remediation.issue: Untrusted learning content can contain secrets or prompt directives
remediation.suggestion: Redact secrets and summarize user-supplied text before logging. Reject entries that tell agents to override policies or change authority.

remediation.issue: Hook-based reminders run in agent context
remediation.suggestion: Keep hooks opt-in, document the exact injected text, and disable PostToolUse unless command output inspection is needed.

remediation.issue: Shell scaffold helper depends on path validation
remediation.suggestion: Keep the relative-path checks and add tests for malicious skill names and output directories.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Agent Instruction Poisoning Risk
semantic_findings.description: The skill encourages agents to promote learnings into CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, SOUL.md, and TOOLS.md. Because those files can become future agent context, untrusted or poisoned learning content could persist as durable instructions without a required review gate.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly name future prompt/context files as promotion targets and recommend aggressive promotion. The risk depends on later review quality, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: AI coding sessions can lose useful corrections, error fixes, and workflow discoveries. This skill records them in structured logs and helps teams promote durable guidance.
actual_capabilities: Creates a .learnings directory with files for learnings, errors, and feature requests.
Defines structured entry formats for corrections, knowledge gaps, command errors, and requested capabilities.
Provides optional hook scripts that remind agents to evaluate learnings after prompts or command failures.
Guides promotion of mature learnings into agent instruction files such as CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.
Includes a shell helper that scaffolds a reusable skill from a validated learning name.
limitations: It does not automatically verify that logged learnings are correct or safe.
Hook behavior is opt-in and depends on local agent support.
The shell helper assumes a Unix-like environment with bash and common command-line tools.
Teams must review entries to prevent secrets or unsafe instructions from becoming persistent context.

use_cases.title: Track debugging discoveries
use_cases.description: Record non-obvious command failures, fixes, and project conventions after a debugging session.

use_cases.title: Share recurring workflow rules
use_cases.description: Promote repeated lessons into shared agent guidance after review and consensus.

use_cases.title: Improve agent handoffs
use_cases.description: Capture patterns that make future Claude, Codex, and Claude Code sessions more consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize learning logs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Create the .learnings files for this workspace if they are missing. Do not overwrite existing content.

prompt_templates.title: Log a corrected assumption
prompt_templates.scenario: Capture a user correction after a task
prompt_templates.prompt: Log the correction from this conversation as a learning. Include the wrong assumption, the corrected rule, and related files.

prompt_templates.title: Review unresolved learnings
prompt_templates.scenario: Find pending items before a larger task
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current learning logs for pending high-priority entries related to this task. Summarize only relevant action items.

prompt_templates.title: Promote mature guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Find recurring resolved learnings that deserve promotion. Draft concise guidance for the correct instruction file and flag security concerns.

output_examples.input: A package install failed because the project uses a different package manager.
output_examples.output: A learning entry notes the mistaken assumption, the correct package manager, related lock files, and a future check.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a missing export feature during a report workflow.
output_examples.output: A feature request entry records the requested capability, user context, estimated complexity, and possible implementation path.

output_examples.input: Several sessions repeat the same build mistake after API changes.
output_examples.output: A promoted guidance draft explains the required post-change step and links back to the resolved learning entries.

best_practices: Log only the useful lesson, not full transcripts or raw secret-bearing output.
Review entries before promotion into persistent agent instruction files.
Use stable IDs, related files, and status fields so future agents can filter entries quickly.
anti_patterns: Do not store credentials, private keys, tokens, or full environment dumps in learning logs.
Do not promote untrusted user text directly into agent instructions.
Do not enable command-output hooks unless the workspace can handle sensitive output safely.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically modify project files?
faq.answer: The main instructions ask the agent to create or append learning files. Hook scripts only print reminders unless separately configured.

faq.question: Can it be used with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents Codex setup through hook configuration and manual learning logs.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Claude Code hook examples and works with standard workspace files.

faq.question: What should not be logged?
faq.answer: Do not log secrets, raw transcripts, private keys, full configuration files, or unreviewed prompt instructions.

faq.question: When should a learning be promoted?
faq.answer: Promote only recurring, reviewed, and broadly useful guidance that helps future sessions avoid the same mistake.

faq.question: Does the extraction helper create a complete skill?
faq.answer: No. It creates a scaffold that still needs reviewed content, examples, and validation before use.
